primitives.name: Snap-to-Whistle Event Segmentation
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Layer 2 — Perception (tracklets → plays) | Module | What it does | |---|---| | `cv-play-segmentation.ts` | Snap-to-whistle detection from tracklet motion energy: pre-snap SET → snap BURST → LIVE → DEAD.
primitives.assumptions: Motion energy follows piecewise deterministic process; whistle detection is binary thresholding of E(t).
primitives.breakdown_regime: Hurry-up scenarios introduce ambiguity in SET→Burst transition due to reduced motion variance.

layer2.mapping: Event segmentation maps to temporal kernel regression: t ↦ E(t) → S(t) via dynamic thresholding.
layer2.telemetry: Temporal alignment accuracy of play boundaries vs. broadcast audio.

primitives.name: Pre-Snap Formation Geometry Classifier
primitives.verbatim_quote: | | `cv-formation-classify.ts` | Pre-snap formation from offense geometry: backfield (under-center/pistol/shotgun/empty), personnel ("11"/"12"/...), distribution (trips/bunch/2x2/3x1).
primitives.assumptions: Offensive geometry is static before snap; formations are categorical with fixed parameter space.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Ambiguous personnel counts under dense coverage or misaligned tracklets.

layer2.mapping: Formation classification uses geometric kernel similarity to canonical templates: F ↦ K(\vec{x}_i, \vec{y}_j).
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy of formation type prediction vs. NFL official records.

primitives.name: Receiver Route Polyline Matching
primitives.verbatim_quote: | | `cv-route-extract.ts` | Per-receiver polylines → 14-route tree via DTW against canonical templates (both lateral mirrors, so dig≠out and post≠corner survive).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R_i': "receiver i's polyline trajectory (meters)", 'T_j': "template j's route (meters)", 'd(R_i, T_j)': 'DTW distance (meters)', 'M': 'mirror symmetry flag (boolean)'}
primitives.assumptions: Routes are modeled as discrete trajectories; DTW preserves topological equivalence under reflection.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Misalignment of receiver tracking leads to false route classification under mirror symmetry.

layer2.mapping: Route extraction is a metric-space embedding: R_i ↦ argmin_j d(R_i, T_j) with M-based refinement.
layer2.telemetry: Precision of route classification against labeled training data.

reasoning_traces.think:
The primitives form a layered signal-processing pipeline where Layer 2 extracts structured events from raw motion data, and Layer 3 accumulates these into statistical tendencies. Play segmentation acts as a temporal filter, formation classification encodes spatial structure, and route extraction provides behavioral dynamics. These map to a hierarchical Bayesian model: P(play|data) ∝ P(data|play)P(play). The failure modes arise from sensor noise, occlusion, and misalignment in tracking, which corrupt the observables and thus the posterior beliefs. Dualities emerge in that each module can be seen as either a feature extractor or a generative model of behavior.
